text:
maya: Heads-up: Product wants to soft-launch Heron (new 13B decoder) to hosted next month. Early perf numbers from bench show ~2.8x tokens/sec per request vs current default, plus median response length ~1.6x. We need a quick capacity estimate for GPU hours and regional impact.

gavin: :eyes: rough numbers?

maya: baseline: current hosted steady-state is ~18k tokens/s global across p100/p4 pools (user-visible). Heron single-model inference latency similar, but token emission rate increases. If traffic shifts 30% of gen calls to Heron, naive token/sec -> +15k tokens/s.
ravi: Wait, 15k extra tokens/s sustained is big. What's our conversion to GPU slots? On p4d a 13B q4 config handles ~500 tokens/s under our batching profile. So 15k -> 30 p4d-equivalent concurrent slots.
lucy: Where did 500 tps come from? which sequence length?
ravi: bench: seq 2048, batch dynamic, KV cache warm. It's an upper bound. With average seq 1024 it's ~600 tps; with short chat (avg 256) it's ~1.8k tps. So depends on user mix.
sre-jen: Region constraints: EU-west has ~40 p4d slots reserved for enterprise. If Heron traffic skews EU by 40% we may saturate EU capacity during working hours. APAC is thinner.

maya: I'm worried about burst days (launch marketing). If we hit 2x baseline peak for 6 hours, that changes GPU-hour estimate. Quick calc: sustained +15k tokens/s for 24h = 1.3B extra tokens/day. Using our cost model ~0.000003 GPU-hour per token? (placeholder) -> ~400 GPU-hours/day. But need concrete mapping.
cost-ops: We shouldn't use placeholder numbers. I'll run a quick cost sim with real pricing. Can you paste the sample log of current per-token GPU-hour mapping?

gavin: Pasting pinned calc from infra-playbook: 
```
# rough mapping used internally
1 p4d-slot @ 48 vCPU workload -> 3.6M tokens/hour (avg seq 1024)
so 1 token -> 2.78e-7 p4d-hours
```

ravi: Using that: 15k tokens/s = 54M tokens/hour -> 15 p4d-hours/hour -> 360 p4d-hours/day. Matches maya-ish.
lucy: Important: that assumes 13B runs at same efficiency. For Heron we saw 0.85x effective throughput vs baseline on p4d due to attention pattern. So bump by ~18% -> ~425 p4d-hours/day.

ops-bot: Note: there is a pending maintenance window in eu-west on 1795100000-1795130000 (reduced capacity by ~25%).

sre-jen: That window lines up with our launch window? maya: product prefers 1795110000 (two weeks out). We should avoid maintenance or shift.

maya: Mitigations: 1) Canary 5% traffic first, 2) Route EU traffic to alternate region for heavy gen paths, 3) Serve short prompts on cheaper quantized variant (Heron-lite), 4) Autoscale aggressive warmup ramp to keep KV caches warm. Thoughts?
gavin: Agree. Also add model-level routing policy: prefer cheapest compatible model unless latency SLO violated. This could cut peak GPU-hours by ~20% based on past rollouts.
cost-ops: If we do 5% canary steadily then 25% ramp over 48h, cost delta first week estimated ~+65% on GPU-hours for gen pipelines. Need approval for short-term budget buffer.
ravi: Actionable asks from infra: (a) capacity reserve request for 450 p4d-hours/day for 2 weeks around launch in hosted pool, (b) setup autoscale policy with prewarm on canary, (c) deploy Heron-lite quantized variant and add routing rule.
sre-jen: Also want a circuit-breaker: if tail latency > 99p 2.5s for 10m, auto-fallback to baseline model. We can plug that into rollout config.
lucy: For simulation, I'll run a traffic replay for last three months with model multipliers and report 5/50/95 pctl GPU demand by region. Expect to have results in 48h.

maya: Cool. Who owns the capacity request doc?
gavin: I can draft the request and send to capacity-ops. Will include EU fallback plan.

cost-ops: If marketing wants to spike traffic, we should plan for burst capacity (on-demand preemptible pool) — cheaper but less reliable. Recommend reserving 150 p4d-hours/day as buffer for first 72h.

maya: Summary of immediate next steps:
- lucy: run replay sims (48h)
- gavin: draft capacity request & budget ask (24h)
- ravi: create autoscale + circuit-breaker rollout config (48h)
- cost-ops: run exact GPU-hour cost numbers and approve short-term buffer (24h)

ops-bot: @infra-oncall FYI: scheduled maintenance conflict noted.

gavin: tagging @sre-jen for the circuit-breaker config review.
sre-jen: I'll review once ravi shares the config. Also please add a smoke test that verifies fallback behavior automatically during rollout.

maya: Thanks all. If the sim looks bad we'll propose delaying the launch by a week. :thumbsup:
